summary.text: A fault is a flat fracture in a body of rock where the rock on either side has shifted a significant distance.
Friction can lock a fault so stress builds up, and when it exceeds the rock's strength the fault ruptures and releases energy as seismic waves, causing an earthquake.
Faults are sorted by how the sides move: the hanging wall drops in a normal fault, rises in a reverse fault, and in a strike-slip fault the sides shift sideways.

facts.label: Locked patches
facts.value: Called asperities, where friction is higher

facts.label: Throw and heave
facts.value: Throw is vertical slip, heave is horizontal

facts.label: Wall names
facts.value: Hanging wall and footwall come from mining

facts.label: Slow movement
facts.value: Faults can also move slowly by aseismic creep

facts.label: Largest faults
facts.value: Form the boundaries between tectonic plates

items.prompt: In a road cut, the rock above a slanted fault has slid down relative to the rock beneath it. What kind of fault is this?
items.explain: In a normal fault the hanging wall, the block above the fault plane, moves down relative to the footwall.

items.prompt: Why can a fault stay quiet for decades and then suddenly produce a big earthquake?

options.label: Magma only pushes up under it now and then
The plates stop moving between earthquakes
Friction holds it while strain slowly builds
Its rocks slowly melt until they can slide

items.explain: A locked fault stores up stress until it exceeds the rock's strength, then ruptures and releases the energy as seismic waves.

items.prompt: A fence crosses a nearly vertical fault. After it moves, the two halves are offset sideways but sit at the same height. What type of fault is it?
items.explain: A strike-slip fault is usually near vertical, and its sides move left or right with very little up-or-down motion.

items.prompt: A long valley floor is a block that dropped down between two normal faults tilting toward each other. What is this block called?
items.explain: A graben is a downthrown block between two normal faults dipping toward each other; a horst is the raised block between grabens.

items.prompt: The terms 'hanging wall' and 'footwall' for the two sides of a sloping fault were borrowed from which line of work?
items.explain: A miner working a tilted ore body stood with one wall under his feet and the other hanging above him.

items.prompt: A region whose crust was being stretched starts being squeezed instead. What can happen to an old normal fault there?

options.label: It locks for good and never moves again
It reactivates and moves the opposite way
It heals over and vanishes from the rock
It turns into a sideways strike-slip fault

items.explain: When stresses reverse, faults can be reactivated with their movement inverted, so a normal fault can become a reverse fault.
